t_psd.why: x87 excess precision in four1/realfft reaching Psd's decibels. Under -fexcess-precision=fast modern GCC keeps 80-bit intermediates the object narrows to 32 bits mid-butterfly, and by the time the transform reaches a decibel the divergence is up to 0.043 dB on bins near -85 dB, where cancellation dominates. It is NOT closable with a tolerance: the smallest separation between two V90PreFilter reference loops that give DIFFERENT answers is SSD 0.00268 dB^2 (AscendNULL vs AscendNULLCodec2, refLoopsType2), a distance of 0.0518 dB, and 0.043 dB on six points moves a signature by 0.105 dB -- four times the separation, so the excess precision can flip autoSelection's winner. `make period` passes all 160: the period compiler has no divergence here, and it is the tier that decides.

checks: agc: process over pole x reference x block x length
t_agc.why: `alpha != T(1)`, the object's frozen test. The object issues ONE ordered compare and no parity test -- `flds (%ecx); fcom %st(3); fnstsw; sahf; jne` at 0xa8 -- and FCOM sets C3 for unordered as well as for equal, so a NaN pole freezes. GCC 13 will not emit that: `-mno-ieee-fp` is accepted and does nothing (measured: `fcomi %st(2),%st; jp; jne`, the parity test intact), and IEEE C requires `!=` to be true for a NaN. `-ffinite-math-only` does remove it and is rejected in finding F2304, because it withdraws NaN semantics from the whole translation unit and eleven `!(a >= b)` sites elsewhere depend on the modern compiler still honouring them. `make period` passes this binary's seven groups and 1,848,336 checks with the object's own compiler and the object's own flags, over the same inputs and not a subset.

t_v90equ.why: The same one-ordered-compare equality as t_agc, at six sites: `linearEquBeta != beta` and `dfeBeta != beta` in the two setters (`flds 0x10(%ebx); fcomp %st(1); fnstsw; sahf; je`, one compare, no parity test), `beta != 0.0f` in each setter's fixed-point arm, and `linearEquBeta != 0.0f` / `dfeBeta != 0.0f` in convertEqualizerToMmx (`fcom %st(1)` against `fldz` and `je`). The other four checks are consequential: enterPhase3, freeze, enterRRN/enterFPE and enterPhase4 all reach one of those six and they went green together on the period tier when the six were corrected. Finding F2300 for the sites, 2304 for why no modern flag closes it. `make period` passes this binary's twenty groups and 208,311 checks.

checks: V92EchoCanceller::process: the sentinel on an unordered out[0]
t_v92ecnan.why: `out[0] == 177.0f`, the sentinel that makes the canceller pass a block straight through.  The object loads the caller's word and compares it against the constant in memory with ONE ordered compare and no parity test -- `flds (%eax)` at .text+0x10f4e, `fcomps <177.0f>` at +0x10f50, `fnstsw %ax; sahf` at +0x10f56, `jne <filter>` at +0x10f59 -- and FCOM sets C3 for an UNORDERED result exactly as it does for an equal one, so `sahf` raises ZF either way and the sentinel arm is taken for a NaN as well as for 177.0f: the block is copied through, the read cursor is stepped, and the adaption is skipped.  IEEE C's `==` is false for a NaN and GCC 13 emits the parity test whatever it is told -- `-mno-ieee-fp` is accepted and does nothing, and `-ffinite-math-only` withdraws NaN semantics from the whole translation unit and breaks eleven sites that depend on them (finding F2304); the two-relational-compare spelling that would satisfy the modern build is two compares where the object has one, and is wrong under the object's own flag (finding F2300).  So the modern build runs the FILTER on a NaN block and every field that arm would have left alone moves with it: 492 of this binary's 2,703 checks fail, all of them two-sided comparisons, while every assertion about what the BLOB did still passes.  IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose.  This check used to be four blocks inside `t_v90leaves`'s `V92EchoCanceller::process` group, where it failed 273 of 4,570 checks and made the whole binary exit non-zero; `tools/mutate.py` judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, so a red binary cannot score a mutation set and refuses -- and FIVE mutation suites are pinned to `t_v90leaves` (`v90cd`, `v90demapper`, `v90rto`, `v90sbe`, `v92ec`; 122 mutations), every one of them unscoreable for this single arm.  Splitting the check out is what that refusal asks for (findings F2157 and F3002), and only the NaN VALUE moved: the blob takes the same path for 177.0f as for a NaN, so `t_v90leaves` still drives every block of every shape and still takes the sentinel arm every seventh block.  `make period` has no allow-list and passes this binary's one group and 2,703 checks with the object's own compiler.

checks: V90AutoDigitalImpDetector::determineMaxUcode: the unordered entry in the window scan
t_v90adidnan.why: `if (v == 0.0f) continue;` in the scan that counts the small entries of a five-entry variance window.  The object compares each entry against a zero it has kept on the x87 stack since 0x4443c and jumps on ZF -- `flds (%eax,%ebx,4)` at .text+0x444d1, `fcom %st(1)` at +0x444d4, `fnstsw %ax; sahf` at +0x444d6, `je` at +0x444d9 -- ONE ordered compare and no parity test, so FCOM's C3 is set for an UNORDERED entry exactly as it is for a zero one and a NaN is skipped along with a zero.  Two small entries beside three NaNs therefore count 2, the window does not qualify, and the answer falls through to the floor.  IEEE C's `==` is false for a NaN and GCC 13 emits the parity test whatever it is told (finding F2304), so the modern build keeps the three entries the object drops, the count becomes 5, the window qualifies and the answer moves: 6 of this binary's 25 checks fail, all of them on the three NaN rows, while both qualifying CONTROL rows and every assertion about what the BLOB answered still pass.  IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose.  This check used to be one row of `t_v90adid`'s `determineMaxUcode` window grid, where it failed 4 of 380 checks and made the whole binary exit non-zero; `tools/mutate.py` judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, so a red binary cannot score a mutation set and refuses -- and `t_v90adid` carries `v90adid` and `v90dil`, 497 mutations and the largest suite in the tree, neither of them scoreable for this single arm.  Splitting the check out is what that refusal asks for (findings F2157 and F3002).  The fourth failing check was not this row but a SEEDED one: `float_9d48` is filled from an LFSR and one trial in sixty-four landed a non-finite word in the window, so `mu_finite_variances` in `t_v90adid` now turns any word whose exponent field is all ones into the largest finite exponent, keeping its sign and significand -- a variance is what that array holds and the object's own writer cannot put a NaN there.  `make period` has no allow-list and passes this binary's one group and 25 checks with the object's own compiler.

checks: V90Phase4Demodulator: the keep-rate flag on an unordered dB
t_v90p4dnan.why: `params->RRN_SILENCE_MIN_ECHO_ENERGY_FOR_KEEP_RATE < dB`, stored into +0x3510 at the tail of CalcErrorEnergyAfterEchoCancellation. The object issues ONE ordered compare and no parity test -- `flds 0x10(%esp); flds 0x404(%ebx); fcompp; fnstsw; sahf; setb %dl` at 0x26956..0x26976 and again at 0x275a0..0x275c6 -- so an UNORDERED result leaves CF set and the flag comes out 1. `dB` is unordered whenever the two silence energies have opposite signs, because then `1.0f / after * before` is negative and `fyl2x` answers a NaN. IEEE C requires a relational compare against a NaN to be false and GCC 13 emits the parity test whatever it is told, so the modern build stores 0 and cannot be made to store 1 from correct source; `-ffinite-math-only` is rejected on finding F2304's ground. THE OPERAND ORDER IS THE FIX AND NOT THE DECLARATION: written `dB > PARAM` the site is wrong under the object's own flag too, which is finding F2301's shape, and t_v90p4ddec's negative-accumulator trial is what caught it. IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose: an excused binary exits non-zero, and tools/mutate.py judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, so a red binary cannot score a mutation set and refuses. Splitting the check out is what that refusal asks for, and it leaves t_v90p4ddec's three sweeps -- 65,984 checks -- green under both compilers and mutation-testable. `make period` has no allow-list and passes all four groups with the object's own compiler.

t_v90equproc.why: x87 excess precision on `float err = soft - fdec` inside `V90Equalizer::process`. The object subtracts two values it has already narrowed to `float` in memory and leaves the DIFFERENCE in a register (`fsub %st(1),%st` at 0x394ef); that difference then feeds the squared-error accumulator, the DFE step and the high-error test, and GCC 3.4.2 spills it -- rounding it back to `float` -- only where a call forces the x87 stack out. Where `soft` is past a short's range the RESET slicer returns the x87 indefinite -32768, so the exact difference needs ONE bit more than a `float` carries and the spilled and unspilled readings part company; half an ulp there is hundreds of counts in `word_78`. THE SAME SOURCE IS EXACTLY GREEN ON THE PERIOD COMPILER: 120,974 differential checks, 0 failed, GCC 3.4.2 at the project's own flags. On GCC 13 it fails 731, and the failures are `word_78`, `word_7c`, `meanErrorEnergyCurrent` and the connection evaluator's average -- every one of them downstream of that one subtraction. IT IS NOT CLOSABLE BY CHOOSING A TYPE, and all three candidates were measured: `long double err` gives 59 on GCC 13 and is wrong on 3.4.2 as well; forcing the narrowing at every use (`volatile float` round trip) gives 733 on GCC 13 and 1 on 3.4.2; the plain `float` the author wrote gives 731 and 0. The object's own behaviour is not expressible portably -- it rounds at some uses and not others, and which is which is the register allocator's -- so the source is the object's, `make period` proves it, and the modern build declares. `-fexcess-precision=standard` would close it and is a translation-unit-wide change to flags this tree derived from the object; finding F1453's t_psd entry is the same class with the same disposition.

t_v90specproc.why: INHERITED, NOT NEW: `V90SpectralVerifier::process` calls `Psd::process` on the sample that completes an accumulation, and `Psd::process` already carries this register's t_psd entry -- finding F1453, x87 excess precision in four1/realfft reaching the decibel scaling, up to 0.043 dB and explicitly not closable with a tolerance. The divergence arrives in this binary as 1 and 2 ULP disagreements in the 32 spectrum bins the periodogram writes: 181 of 35,450 checks on GCC 13, every one of them a `spectrum bin` comparison and none of them a return value, a state, a counter, an accumulation buffer or a transcript. Nothing this binary tests about `process` ITSELF diverges. `make period` passes all four groups and every one of the 35,450 checks with the object's own compiler and the object's own flags, over the same inputs and not a subset -- so the source is right and the modern build is what cannot reproduce it, which is finding F1453's ruling one call deeper. IT IS ITS OWN BINARY on purpose, for the reason t_v90p4dnan's entry gives: an excused binary exits non-zero, tools/mutate.py judges a mutant caught by a non-zero exit, and a red binary cannot score a mutation set. The other seven members of the class are in t_v90specacc.cpp, which is green under both compilers and is where their mutation set lives.
